course: Course 3: Programming in C and Python
reviewer_type: AI review with every program compiled and run by tools/run_chapter.py; no human review yet
title: Bits, Bytes and Number Systems
subtitle: How a computer stores every number and every letter as a pattern of bits, why C's integers wrap around and Python's never do, and how to decode the bytes of a Hindi word by hand.
prerequisite_note: Chapter 1: compiling and running a program in both languages.
objectives: Convert between decimal, binary, hexadecimal and octal, by hand and in code.
Find the sizes and limits of C's integer types, and explain why Python integers never overflow.
Represent negative numbers in two's complement and prove the same adder works for them.
Detect signed overflow in C with the undefined behaviour sanitizer.
Read the bytes of a number in memory and explain byte order.
Encode and decode ASCII and UTF-8 text by hand and in both languages.
